item.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott effectively pauses new data center projects pending statewide grid audit
item.description: Greg Abbott paused new data center interconnection requests as ERCOT reviews over 474 gigawatts of pending applications threatening Texas grid reliability.
item.content:encoded:
Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has ordered state regulators to audit pending data center projects seeking connections to the state's electric grid, a move ERCOT says effectively pauses those projects as Texas grapples with soaring electricity demand driven by artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Abbott on Monday directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to review pending data center projects and deny grid connection requests for facilities that fail to meet state requirements.

ERCOT told Fox News Digital the governor's directive "effectively pauses all data center projects."

"ERCOT is reviewing Governor Abbott's letter concerning data centers and will work with the Public Utility Commission of Texas to implement the Governor's directive, including postponement of the Batch Zero transmission planning study," the grid operator said in a statement.

BLANCHE URGED TO INVESTIGATE ALLEGED FOREIGN INFLUENCE IN FIGHT AGAINST DATA CENTERS

The move comes as Texas sees a surge in demand from artificial intelligence and cloud computing facilities. ERCOT told Fox News Digital that about 90% of the 474 gigawatts of projected large-load interconnection requests currently under review are from data centers — more than five times the state's record peak electricity demand.

"Our top priority is to protect Texans' safety and quality of life," Abbott said in a statement, according to Axios. "Texans must come first."

As part of the review, Abbott directed regulators to gather additional information from companies seeking grid connections, including whether facilities plan to generate some of their own electricity, as well as their projected annual and peak electricity demand, water consumption and water sources.

The directive follows Abbott's recent push to tighten oversight of the rapidly expanding data center industry. Last week, he said AI data centers looking to build in Texas should bring their own power, reuse their own water and lower electricity costs for residents.

THIS RED STATE HANDS REPUBLICANS FRESH AMMUNITION IN THE FIGHT OVER AMERICA'S ECONOMIC FUTURE

Texas has become one of the nation's largest hubs for data center development, thanks in part to generous tax incentives. The Texas Tribune previously reported the state provides more than $1 billion annually in tax breaks for qualifying projects.

Public Utility Commission of Texas Chairman Thomas Gleeson said the agency is working with ERCOT to implement Abbott's directive.

"We appreciate Gov. Abbott's directive and will continue to work closely with ERCOT to ensure these requirements, along with those laid out in our July 17, 2026, letter to Gov. Abbott, are fully carried out on behalf of the people of Texas," Gleeson said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital also reached out to Abbott's office and the Data Center Coalition for comment.

item.title: Goldie Hawn dances in her bathing suit during European family vacation
item.description: Kate Hudson's Instagram video captures Goldie Hawn dancing with an oversized bottle of wine during their family vacation trip to Greece beach.
item.content:encoded:
Goldie Hawn is living it up during her European family adventure.

In a recent Instagram post shared by her daughter, Kate Hudson, the 80-year-old actress, is seen enjoying time with her family while on vacation.

The post features a video of Hawn dancing with a sizable bottle of what appears to be white wine in one of her hands as she makes her way to the other side of the table during a family meal.

She is sporting a one-piece swimsuit with a plunging neckline, which she paired with a long sleeve white cover-up, and a hair clip sticking up from the top of her head.

GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'

"Good sized bottle Goldie, just needs a straw 😂" one fan wrote in the comments section. "Haha! Your Mom is hilarious!" another added.

"I want to be @goldiehawn in my next life 🫶❤️," a third fan said, while another added, "Go Goldie! ❤️😂"

Other photos in the post showed Hudson enjoying time on the beach with her friends and family, as well as the food they ate and them sightseeing.

The "First Wives Club" actress previously made an appearance on Hudson's Instagram reel documenting the family's trip to Greece, which included many clips of Hudson in various bikinis.

Hawn's friend and former co-star, Meryl Streep, recently spoke with Vanity Fair about their time filming the 90s movie, "Death Becomes Her," and why she had "beef" with Hawn on set.

"Goldie, she was always late to set," Streep told the outlet in May. "And I’m always on time, you know, and annoying."

"But she was so adorable," she added. "She had a red convertible, I remember, and she’d drive herself to set. So that was probably the problem. She’d drive herself to set. She had her hair all… ‘Oh gosh, sorry!’ And everybody thought, ‘Oh, she’s so cute.’ Yeah. So I had a beef with her."

Despite their "beef," Streep added that they "just had a lot of fun" filming the movie and that Hawn had "the best laughter in America."

item.title: Man arrested at Trump golf course ahead of president’s visit allegedly had weapons cache
item.description: A man allegedly photographing security preparations at Trump National Golf Club was found with weapons, body armor and concerning notebooks.
item.content:encoded:
A California man was arrested Sunday at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes after allegedly monitoring security-planning activities days before the president’s visit and was later found with a cache of weapons, authorities said.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, of Downey, was arrested Sunday after plainclothes federal agents spotted him walking the golf course grounds, taking photographs and videos while appearing to monitor security-planning activities, according to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department.

Deputies from the Lomita Sheriff's Station responded around 3:30 p.m. and determined Taele was already under investigation for robbery by the El Segundo Police Department.

TWO YEARS AFTER BUTLER, THREATS AGAINST TRUMP KEEP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT IN SHARP FOCUS

During a pat-down, deputies allegedly recovered a 16-round magazine loaded with hollow-point ammunition from Taele's pants pocket. Authorities then searched his vehicle, which was parked in the golf course parking lot, and recovered a loaded pistol with a round chambered, along with another loaded magazine containing hollow-point ammunition.

Taele was arrested on suspicion of carrying a concealed firearm and possessing prohibited ammunition.

The discovery prompted detectives with the Sheriff's Department's Major Crimes Bureau assigned to the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force to obtain a search warrant for Taele's Downey home.

Investigators said they recovered an illegally modified AR-platform rifle, a 1911 .45-caliber pistol, an AR-platform upper receiver, body armor, high-capacity magazines, bulk pistol and rifle ammunition, two radio signal devices and multiple notebooks containing what authorities described as "concerning statements."

The investigation is being conducted jointly by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force and the U.S. Secret Service. Officials said additional charges could be filed as the investigation continues.

Investigators presented the case Tuesday to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office for filing consideration. Taele remains in custody.

Authorities said they have identified no credible threat to the surrounding community but noted the investigation remains active.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the FBI, U.S. Secret Service, the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office, the El Segundo Police Department and Trump National Golf Club for comment.

item.title: Trump admin revokes Brazilian ambassador’s visa in escalating diplomatic feud
item.description: The move follows Brazil’s refusal to grant visas to two U.S. diplomats and its delay in approving President Trump’s nominee for ambassador.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration has revoked the visa of Brazil’s ambassador to the United States amid escalating tensions between Washington and Brasília.

"We communicated continually with the Brazilian government for weeks and have given the Brazilian government every opportunity to do the right thing, yet they have continually delayed and obfuscated," a State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

The spokesperson said Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti has not been declared persona non grata. However, she would have to reapply for a visa if she leaves the U.S.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRACKS DOWN ON BRAZIL'S BIGGEST DRUG GANGS WITH ‘GLOBAL TERROR’ DESIGNATION

The move came after Brazil denied visas to two American diplomats last month and delayed approving former Florida House Speaker Danny Perez, President Donald Trump’s nominee to serve as ambassador to the South American country, according to The Associated Press.

"This is a reciprocal action," the spokesperson said, adding that further diplomatic measures remain possible if Brazil continues to delay or refuses to approve Perez.

Viotti is not being expelled from the U.S. and could resume her duties if Brazil approves Perez, The Associated Press reported.

TRUMP DOJ UNLEASHES LARGEST DENATURALIZATION EFFORT IN DEPARTMENT HISTORY — AND SAYS IT’S ‘ONLY THE BEGINNING’

Last month, Brazil denied visas to Riley Barnes, the State Department's assistant Secretary of State for democracy, human rights and labor, as well as one of Barnes’ top aides, the outlet reported.

The State Department said the pair planned a routine visit to Brazil focused on election integrity, religious freedom and freedom of expression, rejecting claims that they had intended to criticize Lula or the election process.

TRUMP ADMIN BACKS BOLIVIA STATE OF EMERGENCY AS LEFTIST EX-LEADER'S LOYALISTS FRACTURE NATION

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is set to face Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, in the Oct. 4 election, according to The Associated Press.

The dispute also comes as the Trump administration has imposed tariffs of up to 37.5% on thousands of Brazilian exports and designated two major Brazilian drug-trafficking groups as foreign terrorist organizations.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: More than half of some US weapons stockpiles used in Iran war, raising concerns about China threat
item.description: CSIS warns depleted U.S. weapons stockpiles from the Iran war could embolden China as President Xi watches munitions levels amid Taiwan tensions.
item.content:encoded:
Some estimates show the U.S. has used more than half of its stockpiles of some weapons systems in the war with Iran. The Center for Strategic and International Studies found the U.S. has enough missiles to continue fighting in Iran under any plausible scenario, but the group says the true issue with the shrinking stockpiles is future wars.

"We can go on against Iran for quite a long time, even if we've used half the inventory. That means that half the inventories are still available," said Mark Cancian, a retired U.S. Marines colonel and senior advisor with the CSIS Defense and Security Department. 

"The risk is about a future conflict in the Western Pacific against China."

Cancian pointed to reports that military officials have grown more concerned over the U.S. weapons inventory when factoring in other possible conflicts, such as one with China.

WEAPONS STOCKPILE SHORTAGES IMPACTING MILITARY STRATEGY IN THE MIDEAST

"The depletion of munitions was a major topic and a major reason for the suspension of air attacks," Cancian said. "Our inventories were getting way below what the war planners wanted. That might encourage China to do something."

Almost one-third of Tomahawk missiles have been used since the war in Iran began. Nearly two-thirds of Patriot missile interceptors have been depleted. Just over half of precision strike missiles remain. 

President Donald Trump insists the U.S. has plenty of munitions to continue in Iran.

"We have a lot of ammunition, different types," President Trump said in July. "I mean, more than we could ever use, no matter what. But we have a lot. I'd like to have more, to be honest."

HEGSETH DISMISSES ‘FOOLISH’ US STOCKPILE CONCERNS AS IRAN CONFLICT TESTS MUNITIONS

CSIS notes many munition stockpiles are substantial but focused its analysis on seven key weapons that have been effective in Iran and would also be valuable in a possible Pacific conflict.

"We have a defense industrial base that needs to be fixed at a very critical time in our history with the conflict in the Middle East," Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, said. "President Xi of China is watching our stockpiles very closely as he contemplates threatening behavior towards the Taiwan straits, and, so, it all kind of factors in together here. And to be a strong United States, we need a strong military and project strength abroad."

The Pentagon is requesting significant increases in spending for weapons manufacturing, and lawmakers from both sides of the aisle believe the funding is of importance.

TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS

"Look, I have real concerns about our defense industrial base, and God forbid we find ourselves in a lengthy, serious war in our ability to produce what we need," Rep. Chris Deluzio, D-Pa., said. "I actually think it's a place where you can get some cooperation across the parties who want to see us re-industrialize."

The Pentagon’s budget request for fiscal year 2027 includes $5.8 Billion for Tomahawk missiles, an increase of 513% from the fiscal year 2026 request. Proposed spending for precision strike missiles is 245% higher, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAADS) is up 650% and the request for Patriot Missile Segment Enhancement is 927% higher.

"Listen, if it's a $1.5 trillion package for defense, I'm all in. I really am," Rep. Troy Nehls, R-Texas, said. "The munitions are going to be there. We're going continue to do what we have to do to protect the world, protect Israel and everybody else in the region."

If and when the funding is approved, it could take years for the new munitions to reach the battlefield.

"It takes quite a long time for the U.S. to produce new interceptors. They're complex manufacturing assemblages, and thus depleting those stockpiles does leave the U S materially worse off than it otherwise would have been in the current conflict," said UC Berkeley Senior Research Scholar Cameron Tracy.

The Patriot missiles requested in the fiscal year 2027 budget likely will not be available on the front line for another 3½ years. The Tomahawk estimated delivery time sits at almost four years. Some munitions orders could take as long as five years.

FOLLOW US ON X

CLICK HERE FOR MORE U.S. NEWS

"Before the war, it would typically take about two years for the first system to arrive and then another year after that for the last," Cancian said. "You have to sign a contract, and then the manufacturer has to go out with the subcontractors and get all the materials. With the war, those timelines have been extended."

The Trump administration has created framework agreements with contractors to increase production capacity for key munitions. The deals call for new facilities, ambitious timelines and additional weapons systems.

"You can increase production capacity — we are doing that — [for] Patriot and many other systems. First, you have to recruit more people and train them up," Cancian said. "Then you can expand your facilities, but that takes time. You got to build the facilities, and you got to get all the permits and everything else. So, it can be done. We're seeing it happen, but, again, it takes time."

item.title: Michele Tafoya blasts WNBA activism, says Sophie Cunningham is a hero for women's sports
item.description: Michele Tafoya says the WNBA has morphed from a celebration of women's basketball into "activism on display," citing Cheryl Reeve's bench attire.
item.content:encoded:
Michele Tafoya remembers when the WNBA was about celebrating women's basketball.

She told Dan Dakich on "Don't @ Me" that she no longer recognizes the league she once helped broadcast.

Tafoya, who called WNBA games during the league's inaugural years, said politics has replaced the celebration of women's basketball she remembers from the league's early days.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

"I'm losing faith in this league," Tafoya told Dakich. "I have talked about this when this league had its inaugural first three, four seasons, I was one of the three play by play voices. It was Robin Roberts, Hannah Storm and myself and I worked with Reggie Miller and we had a blast. And it was a celebration of these women. This league has now somehow morphed into something that feels like activism on display."

Tafoya pointed to the protest outside a recent Minnesota Lynx game as evidence of how emotionally charged the debate over women's sports has become.

She said pro-trans activists used bullhorns and sirens in an effort to drown out women speaking in defense of female-only competition.

"They (pro-trans protesters) were loud," Tafoya continued. "They had bullhorns. They would press their little siren button and just blast us so we could never talk. It's just hard to believe that we are still conflating this idea of women having their own sport, but trans women somehow having access to that sport when they aren't biologically female.

"This is not an anti-choice, transphobic movement at all. God bless Sophie Cunningham and you know it as well, if not better than I do. She's got a spine. And she is a hero of mine."

TRANS ACTIVISTS HARASS, HURL SLURS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS BEFORE FEVER GAME IN MINNESOTA

Cunningham, one of the WNBA's most outspoken defenders of women's sports, has drawn both praise and fierce criticism for refusing to back down.

When Dakich asked whether her willingness to speak out might encourage other players to do the same, Tafoya admitted today's locker room culture makes that a difficult proposition.

Tafoya also pointed to Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve wearing a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt on the bench, saying it reflected, in her view, a league more interested in pushing activism than promoting basketball.

"I hope it opened the doors for others. But you know what? It's going to be a very narrow group. And the way that the WNBA is responding with Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve wearing a T-shirt, trans kids belong. By the way, this has nothing to do with kids, and I'd love to leave kids out of this entire ideology altogether."

THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID

Tafoya made it clear that, in her view, protecting women's sports is not about hate. It's about fairness, meritocracy and preserving categories women fought decades to establish.

For Tafoya, the WNBA keeps creating distractions of its own making. The more the league leans into activism, she believes, the more the basketball gets lost in the noise.

item.title: Falcons selected two pass rushers in NFL's 2025 draft and neither might be available to start 2026
item.description: The Falcons fear Jalon Walker tore his ACL in training camp, while James Pearce Jr. faces a possible NFL conduct policy suspension to start season.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Falcons had a plan when they selected not one, but two, edge rushers in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft. It almost certainly didn't include opening the 2026 season without either of them.

But that's the strong possibility staring the Falcons in the face now.

It begins with the fact the team fears linebacker Jalon Walker tore the ACL in his left knee during practice on Tuesday.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The club, meanwhile, is holding its proverbial breath as linebacker James Pearce Jr. opened training camp with the specter of an NFL Conduct Policy suspension to start the season hanging over him following offseason legal troubles.

For a club looking to compete in the very winnable NFC South, the uncertainty about their pass rush is now a priority.

The terrible news first:

Walker will have an MRI to confirm the status of his injury suffered in practice on Tuesday. But the club is deeply concerned because tests by doctors on the knee showed a possibility, if not a probability, the second-year player suffered ACL damage.

Walker lay on the field following the injury and his teammates immediately knew something was wrong. Teammates kneeled nearby, some prayed as they looked on, and Walker was eventually carted off the field.

The moment was so emotionally draining and jarring that coach Kevin Stefanski immediately called a halt to the day's practice. The session was cut by about 40-45 minutes.

If the ACL injury is confirmed by the MRI, Walker's 2026 season would be over after only one week of training camp.

ATTORNEY FOR DENVER BRONCOS DEFENDER JONATHON COOPER PLAYS RACE CARD IN DOMESTIC ABUSE CASE

Then there is the serious concern that could make the Atlanta pass rush wobbly on both sides to start the season:

Pearce was arrested Feb. 7 following an incident involving his former girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson.

Pearce was charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, resisting an officer with violence and misdemeanor stalking. Yes, that's a lot.

But in April, once lawyers got involved, Pearce reached an agreement with prosecutors to enter into a six-month pretrial intervention program.

Part of the deal is that it required no admission of guilt by Pearce and carried no jail time. Under the agreement, the charges would be dismissed if Pearce successfully completes all conditions of the program.

So Pearce will not be going to jail and will be able to play if he complies.

But ...

The NFL could nonetheless determine Pearce violated its Personal Conduct Policy.

The league has continued to review the matter and Commissioner Roger Goodell can impose discipline regardless of the outcome of criminal proceedings. The NFL has publicly stated it has been monitoring the case, and Pearce could still face a suspension or other discipline if the league determines his conduct violated its standards.

So, worst case, the Falcons could be without either of its 2025 draft picks to start the season.

The club could turn to backups. Atlanta could also look to add free agent help. But that well is not exactly brimming with possibilities other than veterans such as Joey Bosa or Haason Reddick, who may or may not wish to join a team like the Falcons that have uncertain playoff possibilities.

item.title: First polls close as socialist insurgents eye Midwest gains in Dem civil war
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed and Haley Stevens clash in the most expensive Democratic Senate primary in history, with over $80 million spent and AIPAC at the center.
item.content:encoded:
The polls are now closed in Virginia, one of five states from coast-to-coast holding primary elections on Tuesday.

But the biggest spotlight is on Michigan, where the high-stakes fight between the left-wing and the center-left establishment for the future of the Democratic Party is front-and-center.

Boosted by a string of victories this spring in mostly blue congressional districts across the country, the Democrats' ideological war moves to the Great Lakes battleground state, where progressive victories could reshape the party and endanger must-hold seats in the midterm elections.

Also at stake as Michigan and Virginia join Kansas, Missouri, and Washington State in holding mid-summer primaries is President Donald Trump's immense clout over the GOP and the power of his endorsements in Republican nominating contests.

But taking top billing is Michigan's divisive and expensive Democratic Senate primary, which is seen as the biggest stage to date in the fierce fight for the future of the Democratic Party.

THE MIDTERM SENATE RACES THAT COULD FLIP THE BALANCE OF POWER IN CONGRESS

"This is ground zero in the battle for the future of the Democratic Party, pitting status quo corporate Democrats against shake up the system economic fighters, and we’ll see who wins," Adam Green, co-founder of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee (PCCC), a leading group on the left, told Fox News Digital.

The primary face-off pits Abdul El-Sayed, a former Wayne County Health Department director, against Rep. Haley Stevens, a more moderate candidate backed by the establishment. The race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters, who is backing Stevens, is a must-hold for the Democrats and one of roughly a dozen Senate races from coast to coast that will determine if Republicans hold onto their slim Senate majority.

Matt Bennett, one of the leaders at the Third Way, a leading center-left Democratic organization, told Fox News Digital the Michigan showdown is "the first time the left is competing for a swing seat" and warned, "the significance is it could really put this seat in jeopardy."

El-Sayed, who, if elected, would make history as the nation's first Muslim senator, is an epidemiologist who unsuccessfully ran for governor as an insurgent candidate in 2018. He has made support for "Medicare-for-all" a major component of his campaign.

The far-left candidate has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and is a vocal critic of Israel amid its war with Hamas — even characterizing Israel's actions in Gaza as "genocide" against Palestinians.

MIKE ROGERS ARGUES ABDUL EL-SAYED IS 'A SPECIAL SAUCE OF CRAZY'

And El-Sayed, who is backed by top far-left leaders and teamed with progressive champions Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York on the Michigan campaign trail two weeks ago, and who served as a top surrogate on Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, has vowed not to accept PAC donations.

Stevens, who flipped a GOP-held district in her 2018 election to Congress, is backed by top national and Michigan Democrats, including Peters, term-limited Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, and longtime Senate Democratic Leader Sen. Chuck Schumer.

Schumer and the party establishment view Stevens as more electable than El-Sayed, who has sparked controversy with his past comments.

"I am the best Democrat to go forward. I am the only person in this race who has won tough primaries multiple times. You know, running with the Michigan grit, resilience and determination," Stevens told Fox News Digital on Sunday, as she teamed up with Peters on the campaign trail.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Over $80 million has been spent on the primary showdown, making it the most expensive Democratic Senate nomination race in history. Much of the money has been shelled out by outside groups in support of Stevens and against El-Sayed. The biggest spending comes from United Democracy Project, a political action committee aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC).

El-Sayed, who has repeatedly attacked Stevens over the massive infusion of AIPAC-linked money, told reporters on Sunday, "If you need $70 million to come in here and help get you elected, then the question has to be, are you actually electable on your own terms."

The winner will face off in the midterms against former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers, who is on a glidepath to win the GOP Senate nomination.

The Trump-backed Rogers, who lost the 2024 Senate election in Michigan by a razor-thin margin, said in a Fox News Digital interview that he doesn't care whom he faces off with in November.

"It doesn't matter to us. We've looked at both candidates. We feel confident we're going to beat either one of those candidates that come out of that race," Rogers highlighted.

And Rogers claimed, "They are very radical, and they are way too extreme for Michigan. I mean, Abdul, he has his own special sauce of crazy."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

But Democrats are confident they can regroup after a combustible primary.

"Let's make sure that anyone but Mike Rogers gets to the United States Senate," Stevens told reporters on Sunday. "After the primary, you're going to see a united Democratic Party. You are going to see us going full force, full fledged ahead."

And El-Sayed told Fox News Digital, "I think we all understand the risk of Donald Trump. We all understand the risk of Mike Rogers."

The left-wing versus establishment battle is also playing out in Michigan's 7th Congressional District, a key Republican-controlled swing seat race that's among roughly two-dozen that will impact whether the GOP holds onto its fragile House majority.

William Lawrence, a co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, which advocates for political action to tackle climate change, is on the rise against two more moderate Democrats. Lawrence is backed by Sanders and El-Sayed, as well as some top progressive groups. The primary winner will face GOP Rep. Tom Barrett in the general election.

The party civil war is also on display in Michigan's deep blue 13th Congressional District.

MEET THE FAR LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN THE 2026 MIDTERMS

Rep. Shri Thanedar, who is supported by top House Democratic leaders, is being challenged by state Rep. Donovan McKinney, who is backed by Sanders, El-Sayed, and "Squad" members Reps. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts, and Summer Lee of Pennsylvania.

And the ideological warfare is also front-and-center in Missouri, in the state's St. Louis-based and heavily Democratic 1st Congressional District.

Rep. Wesley Bell is facing off in a rematch against former Rep. Cori Bush, a Squad member who Bell ousted in the 2024 primary.

Trump's endorsements are getting tested in two statewide showdowns on Tuesday, in Michigan and Kansas.

The president is backing Rep. John James in Michigan's GOP gubernatorial primary. James, a West Point graduate and one-time Republican rising star, is facing off against multi-millionaire businessman Perry Johnson, a former gubernatorial and presidential candidate.

The winner will take on likely Democratic nominee and current Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, in the race to succeed Whitmer.

In Kansas, Trump is supporting state Senate President Ty Masterson in a crowded field of Republican gubernatorial contenders.

Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly is term-limited, which makes the race to succeed her a top flip opportunity for the GOP.

In Washington State, the marquee primary showdown is in the state's 3rd Congressional District, where Democratic Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, a former auto shop co-owner, is facing a crowded field of challengers from both parties.

Washington state has a top-two primary system in which all candidates, regardless of party, compete on the same ballot and the two highest vote-getters move on to the general election.

The race is another crucial House showdown that may decide the chamber's majority.

In Virginia, voters head to the polls to cast ballots in Senate primaries and in a handful of House primaries in extremely competitive districts that may impact the balance of power on Capitol Hill.

item.title: Former Disney star Bella Thorne stuns in green sequin bikini during beach day with fiancé
item.description: Bella Thorne stunned in a shimmering green sequin bikini at the beach with fiancé Mark Emms, months after her surprise proposal made headlines.
item.content:encoded:
Former Disney star Bella Thorne took some time to cool off amid the summer heat.

The 28-year-old former child star shared photos of herself enjoying a nice day at the beach in a shimmering green bikini, captioning the post, "it’s getting hot out here.🌶️"

In the photos, Thorne posed for the camera in a green string bikini, which featured large green sequins on the top that glittered in the sunlight.

Some of the photos show her catching some rays and relaxing while laying out on a towel on the sand near the water, while others show her sitting on a lounge chair with her fiancé, Mark Emms.

Thorne also dipped her toes in the crystal clear blue water while posing looking down and away from the camera.

"Sis You look like a beach mermaid 🧜🏻‍♀️😍🔥❤️," one fan wrote in the comments section, while another added, "You are shaking it up on the beach @bellathorne," referencing her former Disney show, "Shake It Up."

The actress recently posed for a series of sultry Instagram photos featuring her in a sheer black lace bra, also surprising fans by ditching her brunette locks and returning to her signature red hair.

She made headlines in August 2025 after she shared with her followers that she got down on one knee and proposed to Emms, two years after he initially proposed to her in May 2023.

Thorne and Emms first met in August 2022 at Cara Delevingne's birthday party in Ibiza. Thorne told Vogue in 2023, "It was love at first sight as the sun rose."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

It didn't take long for romance rumors to start swirling after the two were photographed kissing while on a yacht in Mykonos, Greece. They later went Instagram official in February 2023 and announced their engagement a few months later.

"[We’re] still really learning each other's traits and trying to get them right before we get married so that we're not figuring out all that stuff on the table," she told People in December 2023 about wedding planning. 

"I think me and Mark are really in our language of now, talking it out now, so we can just do it or get through it or decide how we want to feel about it."

item.title: Collins drops the hammer on Trump's pick to lead DOJ, jeopardizing path to confirmation
item.description: Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, says she will vote against Todd Blanche's confirmation as attorney general, citing the anti-weaponization fund and DOJ independence.
item.content:encoded:
The road to confirmation just got bumpier for acting Attorney General Todd Blanche.

After surviving a key committee vote Tuesday, Blanche’s fate became even more uncertain as Republican leaders eye a full floor vote to confirm him. That’s because Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, is not going to back him.

"While I believe Mr. Blanche is a capable lawyer, the Department of Justice (DOJ) has become increasingly political," Collins said in a statement. 

"Mr. Blanche has taken several actions that have further eroded the Department’s independence, and that is the basis for my vote to oppose his confirmation."

TRUMP'S AG PICK SURVIVES — FOR NOW — AS REPUBLICANS QUESTION IF WHITE HOUSE DEAL WILL HOLD

Collins’ decision came after reviewing Blanche’s qualifications to be the replacement for former Attorney General Pam Bondi, including records and his responses during his appearance before the Senate Appropriations Committee that she chairs and his confirmation hearing.

She listed several reasons to go against Blanche, including his approval of a "shield" from IRS audits for Trump, his sons and family and the nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund, which has rankled the feathers of several Republicans since its creation was announced earlier this year.

Collins also pointed to his promises to anti-abortion organizations that he would try to halt mailed abortion medication, his attempted indictments of Sens. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., for their "ill-advised, but constitutionally protected, videos encouraging resistance to unlawful orders" and pushback from over 1,200 Justice Department employees as a basis to buck his nomination.

TRUMP'S AG PICK OFF LIFE SUPPORT AFTER KEY REPUBLICAN REBELS RELENT

"For these reasons, I will vote against this nomination," Collins said.

Her defection is a crucial, but not fatal, blow to Trump and Blanche. Republicans can only afford to lose one more vote before the confirmation is dead in the water.

That’s because Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., is still absent with no clear timeline for his return. And there are more Republicans who are leery of, or not outright saying, that they will support Blanche.

Those include senators Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska; John Curtis, R-Utah; and Bill Cassidy, R-La.

TRUMP THREATENS TO YANK HIS OWN AG NOMINEE AS GOP REVOLT GROWS

It all comes after Blanche and the Department of Justice struck a deal with Sens. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, to win their support in the Senate Judiciary Committee that gave explicit direction that the anti-weaponization fund was dead and narrowed the scope of Trump and his family’s audit immunity.

But critics of the deal in the Senate say there’s no real binding mechanism to ensure that neither Trump nor Blanche would just turn around and tear up the agreement after his confirmation.

It also throws a wrench into Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and the rest of Republican leadership’s plans to try and swiftly confirm Blanche amid a blistering sprint to a near monthlong break for the remainder of August.

Fox News Digital did not immediately receive comment from the White House on Collins' decision.

item.title: Anti-Caitlin Clark ESPN pundit tries justifying claim that Clark isn't among the best guards in WNBA
item.description: ESPN's David Dennis Jr. claims Caitlin Clark still isn't a top-four WNBA guard despite her Player of the Month honors and historic stat lines.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this summer, ESPN racial idolater David Dennis Jr. defended the WNBA players who had hard-fouled and targeted Caitlin Clark. He also argued that Clark wasn't that good and wasn't among the best players at her own position.

"What bothers me is when this is framed as some sort of petty jealousy or insecurity by these women in the WNBA," Dennis began.

"I don't think you can make a compelling argument that Caitlin Clark is a top four guard in the WNBA," he added.

A week later, former WNBA player and NFL analyst Stacey Dales challenged Dennis' argument on-air. She embarrassed him. So much so that he shifted the conversation, claiming Clark's style of play doesn't translate to winning.

Since Dennis made those remarks, Clark has played seven games (July 17 through Aug. 2), averaging 26.1 points and 8.6 assists per game. She won Player of the Month and scored 45 points in one game.

Oh, and she led the Fever to a 6-1 record. So much for her style of play "not translating to wins."

Clark now has seven career games with at least 25 points, 10 assists, and five made 3-pointers. The rest of WNBA history combined has four.

Dennis returned from his X vacation this week (he spent the past few weeks posting on Bluesky) and addressed those mocking him.

He began by declaring that he was "standing by" his previous remarks.

"So: I stand by all the points I made three weeks ago because three weeks ago CC was not a top 4 guard this season. Since then she's put up some of her best games of her career and is on a heater. Some of the other players I had ahead have slumped a bit too," Dennis wrote.

"I think I'd put CC #4 right now. Paige, Olivia and Kelsey are all still above her and there's not really any way I'm coming off that right now. CC is still in the tier right below."

He then took another shot at Clark, this time because of one mediocre game during that seven-game stretch:

"Also another reason these people are unserious is bc they were all in my mentions for two weeks but it's crickets after a game where she was the fourth best guard on the court. If I were a real hater I'd be back at it with them but alas…"

ELLE DUNCAN BLAMES CAITLIN CLARK, HER FANS FOR MEDIA SMEAR CAMPAIGN WHILE IGNORING FACTS

A couple of thoughts.

First, it's important to understand who David Dennis Jr. is. He's one of the few remaining voices at ESPN still clinging to the DEI and BLM era, when the network insisted nearly every story must be viewed through the lens of thinly veiled racism.

Following Ryan Clark's exit, Dennis may be ESPN's most foolish employee left. It's between him and Monica McNutt.

Among Dennis' greatest hits: calling Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle campaign "mortifying," arguing White people have a moral obligation to defend Black people who wrong them, insisting Hulk Hogan should only be remembered as a racist after defending Kobe Bryant despite the credible rape allegation against him, and accusing LSU head coach Lane Kiffin of helping Louisiana "eradicate" Black voting power.

Somehow, ESPN rewarded Dennis with a multi-year contract extension in June. The network hired him in 2021, proudly noting that he was the son of a civil rights activist. What that has to do with sports has never been clear.

So it's fairly obvious why Dennis is so eager to diminish Clark.

The political left has cast Clark as a central villain in the culture war, as the evil, straight White woman thriving in a league of victimized Black lesbians. Dennis is simply following the script.

Still, there's a remarkable level of buffoonery in his analysis.

ESPN WRITER SAYS LANE KIFFIN SHOULD TRY TO STOP LOUISIANA FROM 'ERADICATING' BLACK VOTING POWER

Saying Clark wasn't a top-four guard would have been a hot take. Sports is full of hot takes. However, claiming there wasn't a "compelling argument" for her to be in the top four is where he lost credibility.

And if Clark was supposedly so far behind four other guards just a few weeks ago, how did she suddenly leap into fourth place after a seven-game stretch, as he claims?

He's just saying words. Buzzwords.

Admittedly, debating player rankings is a fruitless exercise. There's no single statistic that settles the debate. Such rankings are inherently subjective.

That said, the consensus around the WNBA is that A'ja Wilson is the league's best player, and Clark is typically ranked somewhere behind her. ESPN itself ranked Clark No. 3 entering the 2026 season, behind Wilson and Kelsey Plum.

We're not here to argue whether Clark is the second-, third-, or fifth-best player in the league. These rankings are not literal. Rather, we are here to point out that Dennis isn't making a serious basketball argument when he insists that Clark is definitively in a tier below Paige Bueckers, Olivia Miles, and Kelsey Plum.

That's not a sports argument. It's a culture-war argument, the kind ESPN should no longer be in the business of making.

Like McNutt, Dennis should soon join Ryan Clark on the growing list of former ESPN personalities who undermined the network with their racial idolatry.

item.title: Florida 3-year-old dies after tragic incident involving common play toy at babysitter's house
item.description: A 3-year-old girl was found unresponsive with her head trapped inside a toy kitchen at a babysitter's home in Boynton Beach, Florida, police said.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida family is mourning its 3-year-old daughter after police said she became trapped in a toy kitchen play set while at a babysitter's home.

The girl, identified by loved ones as Briella, died July 27, four days after Boynton Beach police said she was found unresponsive with her head stuck inside the play set.

Officers rushed to the Meadows of Boynton Beach community shortly after 11 a.m. on July 23 after receiving a report of a child who was not breathing.

Police immediately began life-saving measures before Boynton Beach Fire Rescue transported the toddler to a nearby hospital, where she remained in critical condition until her death.

DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED

Investigators said the 3-year-old and her sibling were at a babysitter's home when the incident happened.

According to Boynton Beach police, the babysitter had left the residence and placed the children in the care of the babysitter's spouse.

While the children played downstairs, the spouse remained upstairs, periodically checking on them and bringing them snacks, police said.

TENNESSEE WOMAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO DROWN ONE OF HER CHILDREN IN BACKYARD POOL

During one of those checks, the spouse found the toddler with her head stuck inside the toy kitchen, police said.

The spouse freed the child and immediately began performing life-saving measures until first responders arrived.

Police said the child's sibling told investigators that some of the children's toys had fallen inside the play kitchen. The toddler apparently became trapped while trying to retrieve them.

Authorities have not announced any criminal charges, and the investigation remains ongoing.

In a GoFundMe created following Briella's death, loved ones remembered the little girl as "a bright light in the lives of so many."

"She had a kind heart, a beautiful spirit, and a smile that could light up any room," the fundraiser said. "She touched countless lives with her love, laughter, and compassion, and the impact she made will never be forgotten."

The fundraiser said donations will help the family cover funeral and memorial expenses as they navigate the devastating loss.

"She will forever be loved, forever missed, and forever in our hearts," the fundraiser said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Palm Beach County Medical Examiner's Office for the toddler's cause and manner of death but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Jerry Jones 'open' to co-owning Cowboys with Mark Cuban: 'All the respect in the world for him'
item.description: Jerry Jones says he's open to Mark Cuban's private equity firm Harbinger co-owning the Dallas Cowboys, as the $13 billion franchise could eye a minority stake sale.
item.content:encoded:
A two-headed monster in the Dallas Cowboys' headquarters is not out of the question.

Jerry Jones has built the Cowboys into the multibillion-dollar "America's Team," but he's "open" to having another local legend by his side.

Jones told The Dallas Morning News that he would be "open" to former Dallas Mavericks majority owner Mark Cuban co-owning the team through his private equity firm, Harbinger.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Cuban, too, told the outlet that he was "sure our Harbinger fund would be open" to the idea.

"That’s exactly why if you’re me, you would be open to that is because of the man. I have all the respect in the world for him and I know what he did for the Mavericks and what he’s done for basketball," Jones told the Dallas Morning News. "He’s in additional to financial boatstreams of your team, you want to associate with the highest quality of [a person] who loves the game and then also at the same time wants to do something about it. Mark leads the way in that."

TEXANS' JALEN PITRE NAMED FIRST-EVER NFL GUARDIAN CAP ATHLETE IN LEAGUE HISTORY: 'EVOLUTION OF THE GAME'

NFL owners approved a measure two years ago that allowed private equity firms to purchase between 3% and 10% of a franchise.

Jones' comments come days after his son, Cowboys chief operating officer Stephen, said the family "wouldn't rule...out" selling a portion of the team.

"But we’d also be very particular in who we would bring in as a partner in terms of that," the younger Jones told 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

Cuban still owns 27% of the Mavs.

The Cowboys' $13 billion estimated valuation is the largest in all of North American professional sports, according to Forbes.

Cuban sold nearly 75% of his team in December 2023 for a $3.5 billion valuation. His fund also recently purchased a minority stake in MLB's Athletics, which are set to play in Las Vegas in 2028.

item.title: Kentucky child killer walks free as family says justice failed despite years of legal fights
item.description: Ronald Exantus walked free after serving his sentence for the 2015 home invasion that killed 6-year-old Logan Tipton despite Logan's Law reforms.
item.content:encoded:
The Kentucky father whose 6-year-old son was stabbed to death while sleeping says the man found not guilty by reason of insanity in the killing received "a slap on the wrist" after being released from prison July 29 upon completing his sentence for assaulting three surviving family members.

Ronald Exantus was released from Kentucky Department of Corrections custody July 29 after completing the sentence imposed for assaulting Logan Tipton's father and sisters during the 2015 home invasion that left the 6-year-old dead.

The case stunned Kentucky after prosecutors said Exantus broke into the Tipton family's home on Dec. 7, 2015, and fatally stabbed 6-year-old Logan Tipton while he slept. Logan's father and two sisters were also stabbed but survived the attack. A jury later found Exantus not guilty by reason of insanity on murder and burglary charges but guilty but mentally ill on assault charges involving the surviving family members.

The assault convictions resulted in the prison sentence he completed last week, reigniting outrage from the Tipton family and renewed questions about Kentucky's criminal justice system.

FLORIDA AG SEEKS JUDGE'S IMPEACHMENT AFTER BABY DROWNING COVID INSANITY ACQUITTAL

"The judge and jury gave this monster a slap on the wrist while handing down a life sentence to my family," Logan's father, Dean Tipton, wrote on Facebook after Exantus' release. "Make sure to lock your doors and keep an eye out for baby killers. He will be released today. Watch your house, your neighbors house, your kids, your neighbors kids. He could be coming to your town. Kentucky justice at its finest."

According to the Kentucky Department of Corrections, Exantus completed the sentence imposed by the court after receiving sentence credits required under Kentucky law.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

"Ronald Exantus has served the sentence issued by the Woodford Circuit Court and has been released," the department told Fox News Digital. "He is no longer in the custody of the Department of Corrections."

Corrections officials emphasized that juries and courts determine an offender's sentence, while the department is responsible for calculating that sentence under Kentucky law, including applying any earned statutory sentence credits.

Once Exantus reached his legally calculated sentence expiration date, the agency said it no longer had authority to keep him incarcerated.

The department also stressed that the Kentucky Parole Board "did not release Exantus, and he was not released early."

Exantus was briefly released on mandatory reentry supervision in October 2025 before moving to Florida, where authorities said he violated the conditions of his supervision by failing to register as a convicted felon.

He was returned to Kentucky after the violation, and the Parole Board revoked his mandatory reentry supervision, ordering him back to prison. The department said he ultimately remained incarcerated until completing his sentence July 29.

NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'

Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman said his office worked alongside prosecutors, law enforcement and corrections officials to keep Exantus incarcerated for as long as the law allowed.

In a November 2025 letter to the Kentucky Parole Board, Coleman urged board members to revoke Exantus' mandatory reentry supervision after Exantus violated its conditions in Florida and required him to serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.

"The public good and common sense demand nothing less," Coleman wrote, calling Logan Tipton's killing "every parent's worst nightmare."

The Parole Board ultimately revoked Exantus' mandatory reentry supervision and ordered him back to prison after finding he violated the terms of his supervision.

Ahead of Exantus' scheduled release, the Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet also notified the trial judge, Commonwealth's Attorney Kelli Kearney and defense counsel that they could pursue involuntary hospitalization proceedings before his sentence expired if they believed it was appropriate under Kentucky law.

The Department of Corrections said it lacked the legal authority to continue holding Exantus once he completed his sentence unless another lawful basis for detention was established.

In a November 2025 interview with WKYT, Coleman said "the system failed the Tipton family," while pledging to pursue every legal avenue available to keep Exantus incarcerated.

CALIFORNIA MOM RIPS NEWSOM-BACKED 'DIVERSION PROGRAM' THAT APPEARS TO BENEFIT HER SON'S KILLER

Public outrage over Logan’s case helped spur Kentucky lawmakers to pass House Bill 422, known as Logan’s Law, which Gov. Andy Beshear signed in April.

The law revised Kentucky’s insanity defense and mandatory reentry supervision rules in response to issues raised by Exantus’ case. But because it does not apply retroactively, it had no effect on Exantus' sentence or July 29 release.

State Rep. Daniel Fister, who helped champion the legislation, called Exantus' release "heartbreaking" and vowed to continue working with the Tipton family to strengthen Kentucky's criminal laws.

"My heart breaks yet again for the Tipton family and our community as we are once again forced to endure the pain and uncertainty caused by Ronald Exantus," Fister told Fox News Digital.

NORTH CAROLINA TEACHER'S KILLING REIGNITES SCRUTINY OF ROY COOPER'S CRIMINAL JUSTICE RECORD IN SENATE RACE

"No family should have to endure this kind of trauma, and every Kentuckian deserves confidence that our justice system will protect innocent victims and hold violent offenders accountable."

Fister said Logan's Law was "an important step forward" but promised lawmakers would continue pursuing reforms to better protect Kentucky families.

"We owe it to Logan's memory and to every family across the Commonwealth to continue pursuing reforms that put the safety of innocent Kentuckians first," he said.

Fister also said Exantus' release underscores broader concerns about Kentucky's criminal justice system, arguing that delays in implementing provisions of House Bill 5 have allowed some violent offenders to become eligible for parole earlier than lawmakers intended.

DEVASTATED MOTHER BLAMES SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICIES AFTER CAREER CRIMINAL IS CHARGED IN SON’S DEATH

"That is deeply troubling for victims and their families who deserve confidence that violent criminals will be held fully accountable," he said.

State Rep. T.J. Roberts, who also helped author Logan's Law, called Exantus' release "a gross miscarriage of justice."

"Once again, Kentucky's judiciary has failed the Tipton family," Roberts told Fox News Digital. "The monster who killed Logan Tipton should spend the rest of his life in prison, at a minimum, and his release is a gross miscarriage of justice. The Tipton family, all of Kentucky, and all of America deserve so much better than what this government offers to the innocent."

Roberts noted that the U.S. Constitution prohibits lawmakers from retroactively increasing criminal penalties, meaning Logan's Law could not be applied to Exantus after his conviction.

GIANNO CALDWELL: FOUR YEARS AFTER MY BROTHER’S MURDER, I’M MARCHING FOR JUSTICE

Calling Logan's Law "a great first step," Roberts said he plans to introduce additional legislation that would expand the availability of life without parole for murder convictions, strengthen victim notification requirements and further protect Kentuckians from violent offenders.

"I intend to file legislation to ensure our justice system protects the innocent, not violent offenders," he said.

Roberts also offered a message directly to the Tipton family.

"I want the Tipton family to know they have my support and the support of millions of people who have heard their story," he said. "God is with them, and we will not let Logan's life be forgotten."

BODYCAM FOOTAGE FUELS BACKLASH AFTER POLICE HANDCUFF DYING STABBING VICTIM

For Tipton, Exantus' release reopened wounds that have never healed.

"Knowing that this monster gets to walk free and live his life, while I lay in this bed and my baby boy is in the grave," he wrote. "This may be my breaking point."

Although Logan's Law has now taken effect, Tipton said he believes Kentucky must go further.

"So I've come to terms that even though we got Logans Law passed it is still not enough," he wrote. "Violent criminals should not be able to knock so much time off their sentence.

"Our judicial system as a whole needs to be over hauled and I am gonna fight for more change."

Despite helping inspire Logan's Law, the Tipton family says its fight is far from over. The family has launched a GoFundMe to help pay for attorneys as they pursue additional legal remedies and continue pushing for further criminal justice reforms.

"We turned our deepest grief into a fierce, relentless battle to change the law so no other family would ever have to suffer the way we have," the family wrote on the fundraising page. But while Logan's Law was signed this year, they noted it "does not retroactively stop our son's killer from being released."

"The fight is not over and we need your help," the family added.

item.title: Rosie O'Donnell won't worry about FCC, Brendan Carr ahead of Kimmel hosting, doesn't 'pay any heed to them'
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell dismissed FCC Chairman Brendan Carr and his agency as a threat ahead of her upcoming "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" guest hosting stint later this month.
item.content:encoded:
Rosie O'Donnell told Kara Swisher Monday that she isn't worried about the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) or FCC Chairman Brendan Carr ahead of a guest hosting stint on ABC's "Jimmy Kimmel Live!"

The former TV personality discussed her plans for appearing on Kimmel's show on Swisher's podcast. The conversation eventually led to O'Donnell's ongoing feud with President Donald Trump and whether his administration could go after the broadcast.

"Let me ask you, are you worried that Trump, speaking of doing things, he'll obviously be watching you because he's riveted to you in some fashion... Are you worried about any FCC?" Swisher asked. "They went after ABC. They went after ‘The View.’ They're continuing to go after 'The View,' but are you worried about the FCC under Brendan Carr?"

JIMMY KIMMEL REVEALS HE ASKED MAJOR TRUMP CRITIC TO GUEST HOST WHILE HE'S ON VACATION AS A 'SPECIAL TREAT'

"Doing what?" O'Donnell asked.

"Coming after you on the show, for example, doing anything?" Swisher clarified.

"No. What are they going to say? That you can't say that?" O'Donnell said.

Swisher claimed that Carr, whom she referred to as a "moron," was "saying" things like that, but O'Donnell continued to dismiss him as a threat.

"Well, I don't listen to them. I don't pay any heed to them," O'Donnell said.

Though she did not express any concern regarding repercussions for her time as host, O'Donnell revealed that the network had already rejected her Trump-related parody of the "Wizard of Oz" song "If I Only Had a Brain."

ROSIE O'DONNELL REVEALS SHE WILL RETURN TO 'THE VIEW' FOR ANNIVERSARY, DETAILS TENSION WITH WHOOPI GOLDBERG

"I wanted to do that on Kimmel, but they just told me I can't, that they couldn’t get permission for the parody because it’s political content. And I was like, 'Well, that is absurd to me because we used to do parodies every day on my show,'" O'Donnell said.

A source familiar with the situation informed Fox News Digital that the song has not yet been rejected but is instead in the process of copyright clearance.

Fox News Digital also reached out to the FCC for comment.

O'Donnell is set to host one week of episodes for Kimmel's talk show beginning Aug. 17 during the host's two-month vacation. Other guest hosts, according to Kimmel, will include Tiffany Haddish, Colman Domingo, Ike Barinholtz, Anthony Anderson and Jelly Roll.

In 2025, Carr issued a threat against ABC and its parent company Disney, citing the potential "avenues" the FCC could pursue after Kimmel sparked outrage for his comments regarding Charlie Kirk's assassination. After companies like Nexstar Media Group and Sinclair Broadcast Group vowed to ban "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" on its stations following his comments, Disney announced it would preempt his show "indefinitely" before the show eventually returned to air one week later.

ABC FIRES BACK AT FCC PROBE OF 'THE VIEW,' CALLS OUT AGENCY'S 'CHILLING EFFECT ON FIRST AMENDMENT'

In an interview with Fox News Digital in February, Carr said that he feels "no regrets" for his original comments and instead felt glad that local stations and affiliates pushed back against corporations like Disney.

"In fact, I want to see more of that," Carr said. "I think these local affiliates have become simply mouthpieces in too many cases for Disney and other national programmers. I don't think we're better off as a country for that. And so I really want to see those local TV stations actually serve the needs of their community."

item.title: WNBA silent on Clay Travis offer to pay Las Vegas Aces $10 million to beat high school boys team
item.description: WNBA and WNBA champions both silent in response to Clay Travis offer of $10 million to the Las Vegas Aces to play a high school boys basketball team.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA has once again found itself embroiled in controversy, thanks in large part to the reaction from Sophie Cunningham's comments on male competition in women's sports.

When Cunningham said that transgender male athletes should not compete in women's sports, she echoed a position shared by 80% to 90% of the American public. And also one supported by the realities of biology and science considering the inherent physical advantages men have over women.

But her remarks set off a firestorm of criticism and backlash within the WNBA. Players, coaches, fans... all rushed to critique those comments, boo Cunningham whenever she touched the ball, or wear pointed clothing specifically in response to her statement. Several feigned ignorance of the science behind males in women's sports. One co-owner was even suspended after confronting a young Cunningham supporter.

CLAY TRAVIS UPS OFFER TO $10 MILLION FOR WNBA CHAMPION LAS VEGAS ACES TO PLAY HIGH SCHOOL BOYS BASKETBALL TEAM

In order to educate those curiously uninformed coaches, OutKick founder Clay Travis publicly posted an offer to the WNBA: have the Las Vegas Aces, the league's championship winning team, play a high school state title-winning boys' basketball team, with $10 million at stake. Beat the boys, get $10 million. For a team with an estimated annual revenue of $33 million, that's a substantial sum of money. Forbes even estimated the Aces were worth $300 million in 2025, meaning the $10 million prize would represent about 3.3% of the franchise's valuation.

Yet more than 24 hours later, there's been radio silence. Both from the league, from those coaches who are more than ready to jump in to defend left-wing politics whenever necessary, and from the Aces themselves.

OutKick then reached out to both the WNBA and the Aces organization to ask whether they'd consider Travis' offer. And, as of the time of publishing, had received nothing but the same radio silence. Which raises the question: Why? Why not respond? Why not play the game? Travis posted an update on Tuesday that says there are teams "across the country" reaching out wanting to participate. While also revealing why the Aces won't.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"High school boys teams across the country are reaching out wanting to play the WNBA champ Las Vegas Aces," he wrote. "But the Aces are silent. Tells you everything. They know they would get smoked. But men should definitely be allowed to play in their league per coaches. Such a joke."

That's precisely the problem. The league, the players, the coaches, the Aces... they all know what the outcome would be. Which doesn't mean that the WNBA isn't worth watching for its fans, or that the women who play in it aren't extremely talented athletes in their own right. But it's clear that the WNBA exists because there are differences between men and women. Nobody's asking them to downplay their own talent, they're asking for a sports league to acknowledge the most basic tenets of objective reality. And they can't do it, because their commitment to left-wing politics comes first.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Travis also posted asking why the "WNBA (won't) just issue a statement saying only players born as women are eligible to play in their league? The Olympics and women’s tennis have done it. Caitlin Clark asked the league to make a statement. Seems pretty easy to do. Why the silence?"

That's it. That's not an enormous lift. It's not an unreasonable ask. It's the only justifiable position to maintain competitive integrity. And they can't do it, and they won't do it. Losing to an elite high school boy's basketball team wouldn't be embarrassing. But their complete and utter silence sure is.

item.title: Neighbors say riders' screams from Universal coaster pierce their windows day and night
item.description: Angry residents say screaming from riders on Universal Studios Hollywood's new "Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift" roller coaster echoes through their neighborhood day and night.
item.content:encoded:
Universal Studios Hollywood's new "Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift" roller coaster is already drawing complaints from nearby residents over its noise as the attraction undergoes technical rehearsals ahead of its official opening. 

Capable of reaching speeds of up to 72 mph, the outdoor coaster has brought backlash from neighbors, who say screams from test riders have echoed across the nearby Toluca Lake community, as Fox 11 Los Angeles reported.

A Universal Studios Hollywood spokesperson told Fox News Digital the venue is actively reviewing sound levels as technical rehearsals continue. It said the company values feedback from nearby residents.

NEW JERSEY COASTAL CITY CLASHES OVER PROPOSAL TO TRANSFORM AMUSEMENT PARK INTO LUXURY HOTEL

"We appreciate hearing from the community, and that feedback is an important part of the process," a Universal Studios Hollywood spokesperson said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. 

"The coaster is currently in technical rehearsals. As part of that process, we are actively reviewing sound levels."

The more than 4,100-foot attraction is Universal Studios Hollywood's first high-speed outdoor roller coaster. It uses 360-degree rotating ride vehicles inspired by the "Fast & Furious" film franchise, according to Universal Studios Hollywood’s website.

item.title: Senators coach reveals that even he was surprised by team's blockbuster Brady Tkachuk trade
item.description: Travis Green admits he was surprised and even a little mad when Brady Tkachuk was traded to the Florida Panthers after taking the Ottawa Senators job.
item.content:encoded:
One of the most shocking parts of this NHL offseason — and there have been a few of them — came when the Ottawa Senators shipped captain Brady Tkachuk down to the Florida Panthers.

It came just weeks after Tkachuk insisted he was committed to the team.

And, in fact, it was so shocking, even Senators head coach Travis Green says he was surprised by it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"It was probably about a month after the season, three weeks that (Senators GM Steve Staios) brought me up to speed, and he asked me if I was surprised," Green recalled during an appearance on Daren Millard and John Shannon's 100% Hockey podcast. "Oh man, a little bit, of course."

Green — who previously coached the Vancouver Canucks and New Jersey Devils — said that the Senators' young core, which included Tkachuk, was one of the reasons he took the job in the Canadian capital.

So to hear that he had asked to be traded and he was going to be moved at some point — you know, unfortunate is a word I probably will use a lot," Green said. "I can't speak for Brady; I was a little surprised; a little, you know, would I say mad? A little bit."

Honestly, can you blame him?

SOCIAL MEDIA REACTS TO RED WINGS AWKWARDLY WISHING DYLAN LARKIN A HAPPY BIRTHDAY AFTER HE REQUESTED A TRADE

While things had gotten tough for Tkachuk at the end of his time in Ottawa, there's no question that the Sens are a team on the rise. They made the playoffs this season, and while they got waxed by the eventual champion Carolina Hurricanes (honestly, who didn't though this year), it showed a serious step in the right direction.

So, to lose a centerpiece like Tkachuk is tough.

But...

There's no question that, whether it was legitimate or fueled by the media, the attention around Tkachuk's status with the team was a distraction.

One that the team doesn't have any longer.

So, perhaps that will help them make another run to the playoffs again. The team brought in Andre Burakovsky and William Eklund, which rounds out a solid lineup that includes Tim Stützle, Drake Batherson, Shane Pinto, Jake Sanderson, Dylan Cozens and some veteran leadership from Claude Giroux, who signed a one-year deal to return to Ottawa last month.

item.title: Air Force says two advanced stealthy aircraft are ahead of schedule, with first delivery set for 2027
item.description: The B-21 Raider stealth bomber program accelerated 25% after a $4.5 billion funding boost, with Northrop Grumman targeting seven bombers annually.
item.content:encoded:
The Air Force says its next-generation B-21 Raider stealth bomber program is ahead of schedule, with the first operational aircraft expected to arrive at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 2027.

The service's sixth-generation F-47 fighter is also progressing faster than expected, according to Gen. Dale White, director of Critical Major Weapon Systems, who discussed both programs during the Air Force's Life Cycle Industry Days conference in Dayton, Ohio.

White said the B-21 acquisition program has accelerated by roughly 25% since a one-time $4.5 billion funding boost was included in the 2025 reconciliation bill.

The comments provide one of the clearest public updates yet on the status of the Air Force's two flagship next-generation aircraft programs.

AMERICA’S NEW STEALTH B-21 RAIDER TAKES NEXT STEP WITH SECOND BOMBER’S FIRST FLIGHT

The update comes months after the Air Force announced a second B-21 Raider joined flight testing at Edwards Air Force Base in California, a milestone officials at the time said would accelerate testing and weapons integration for America's first new long-range bomber in more than three decades.

White said the first operational B-21 is expected to be "on the ramp" at Ellsworth in 2027, with Northrop Grumman planning to eventually produce seven operational bombers annually. The Pentagon has requested $6.1 billion for the B-21 program in its fiscal year 2027 budget proposal.

Built by Northrop Grumman, the B-21 is designed to carry both conventional and nuclear weapons while penetrating advanced enemy air defenses. The aircraft is expected to eventually replace the B-1 Lancer and B-2 Spirit while operating alongside modernized B-52 Stratofortress bombers expected to remain in service into the middle of the century. The Air Force plans to acquire at least 100 B-21 bombers.

White also said planning for the Boeing-built F-47 has reached an "unprecedented maturity."

INSIDE AMERICA’S 6TH-GEN ARSENAL: B-21, F-47, AND THE FUTURE OF AIR DOMINANCE

The Air Force plans to acquire 185 F-47 fighters, with the first flight scheduled for 2028. The aircraft will replace the F-22 Raptor as the service's primary air superiority fighter and is expected to operate alongside Collaborative Combat Aircraft, autonomous "loyal wingman" drones designed to support crewed aircraft in combat. The Pentagon has requested $5.03 billion for the F-47 program in its fiscal year 2027 budget request.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Air Force, Northrop Grumman and Boeing for comment.

item.title: WNBA coach torches league’s officiating after latest bizarre no-call: ‘It’s a f------ joke’
item.description: Tyler Marsh called it a joke after Kamilla Cardoso took 15 shots without a single free throw, adding to growing frustration over WNBA officiating.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Sky head coach Tyler Marsh didn’t attempt to hide his frustration with WNBA officials following Monday night’s loss to the Phoenix Mercury.

Marsh was asked how Kamilla Cardoso, a 6-foot-7 center, managed to play 28 minutes, take 15 shots and battle inside throughout the game without attempting a single free throw.

"That was a joke. It’s a f------ joke. It’s a joke," Marsh said. "How many more games does she need to go without getting a free throw? It makes no sense. Zero sense."

Cardoso finished with 16 points, 13 rebounds and five assists in Chicago’s 106-101 loss. She made eight of her 15 field-goal attempts, but never went to the line. The Mercury attempted 40 free throws compared to 25 for the Sky.

CAITLIN CLARK CALLS FOR FULL-TIME WNBA REFEREES AS OFFICIATING FAILURES MOUNT IN 2026

Marsh made clear that he wasn’t blaming the officials for the loss or suggesting Phoenix received 40 undeserved attempts. In fact, he admitted Chicago had been too undisciplined defensively.

"We fouled our asses off today. We could have been more disciplined," Marsh said. "Not saying the officials made 40 wrong calls or 20 wrong calls, whatever it is. Not saying that at all."

His complaint centered on Cardoso, who averages nearly 10 field-goal attempts per game but fewer than four free-throw attempts despite operating primarily around the basket. Marsh has raised the issue repeatedly and said last week that "the film doesn’t lie" about the amount of contact Cardoso absorbs.

Perhaps Marsh is exaggerating when he argues Cardoso should get close to 11 free throws every night. Coaches advocate for their players. That’s part of the job.

But zero?

That’s difficult to explain, particularly in a league that has spent much of the season trying to explain its officiating.

Marsh’s outburst might be dismissed as one frustrated coach defending one of his players if it happened in a vacuum. But it didn’t.

In June, Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas drove her fist into Caitlin Clark’s throat during a scramble for a loose ball. The officials didn’t call a foul.

The WNBA reviewed the play the following day, determined Thomas had committed a "non-basketball act," assessed a Flagrant Foul 2 and suspended her for one game.

In other words, the league decided the play was serious enough to warrant an ejection-level penalty and a suspension, but three officials watching it happen in real time didn’t see anything.

Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White called the no-call "absolutely egregious and utterly disrespectful."

The WNBA’s decision to punish Thomas after the fact validated White’s criticism. It also raised an obvious question: How does a player get struck in the throat in front of multiple officials without one of them blowing a whistle?

Then, on Sunday, Sophie Cunningham took an elbow to the face from Minnesota Lynx forward Nia Coffey.

Referees called a foul against Cunningham.

Officials reviewed the play but didn’t change the initial call, leaving the foul assessed to Cunningham despite her being the player who took an elbow to the mouth.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TAKES VICIOUS ELBOW TO FACE, AND FANS FUME AT WHAT REFS DID NEXT

Clark is the biggest draw in the league and Cunningham has become one of its most recognizable and polarizing players. Yet, WNBA officials missed a fist to Clark’s throat and managed to penalize Cunningham for getting hit in the face.

Now Marsh is publicly asking how Cardoso, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, can spend an entire game operating around the basket without earning one free throw.

The league knows officiating has become a problem and major errors involving some of the league's biggest stars are drawing more attention to the issue.

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert devoted a significant portion of her All-Star media availability to the issue, acknowledging that the league "always" needs to improve its officiating.

She said the league reviews every call, non-call and significant non-call, and announced that the WNBA plans to launch a fully centralized replay center in 2027.

Engelbert said the investment, which will cost tens of millions of dollars, is intended to create more consistency, efficiency and transparency.

That sounds good. It also doesn’t do much for players getting hit in the throat or face in 2026.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

The WNBA hasn’t committed to implementing the NBA’s Last Two Minute reports, which publicly identify correct and incorrect calls in the closing minutes of close games. So, while the league promises more transparency through a replay center next season, it still isn’t prepared to offer the type of public officiating accountability its NBA counterpart already provides.

Replay has its limits, too. Officials reviewed the Cunningham play and still left the foul on the player who got elbowed. The Clark play never even reached an in-game review.

A centralized replay center won’t fix much if officials fail to review obvious contact in the first place, or review it and still get the call wrong.

Marsh wasn’t arguing that officiating cost Chicago the game Monday. White’s complaints didn’t change the result of Indiana’s loss to Phoenix, either. But that’s not the point.

The issue is that coaches, players and fans continue to watch obvious contact treated completely differently from one game to the next.

Heck, sometimes it seems like the rules change from one possession to the next.

A replay center might help in 2027.

For now, the WNBA has a player punched in the throat with no foul, another called for a foul after taking an elbow to the face and a 6-foot-7 center who couldn’t get to the line once while taking nearly all her shots in the paint.

Marsh called it a "f------ joke."

At this point, he’s hardly alone.

item.content:encoded:
We've been here before. We've had married prison guards in hot water for alleged affairs with inmates. A lot of these tales of following one's heart into situations they can't win have taken place overseas.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

There was talk of "vibrating panties" and "big man hands" in one of the alleged dirty exchanges, according to the criminal complaint.

Pensak is alleged to have started the intimate relationship with the unnamed inmate sometime after she started working in his unit in 2024. They're accused of having sex in an office with paid inmates serving as lookouts.

This is a reminder that there's no place for romance to hide. These two found each other somehow and made memories. Memories that have landed the married prison guard into a lot of trouble.
